clue.text: Tramp wrapped in paper sheets has got large bottle

indicators.note: the tramp is enclosed by the paper, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper sheets, nominally 500
a hobo is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A vagrant swaddled in newspaper clutches a big bottle of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a wine or champagne bottle holding about six standard bottles' worth.

clue.text: Multi-faceted girl chased by hack

indicators.note: something chased by another has the second coming after it, so the girl comes first

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
to hack is to cut roughly

explanation.surface: A girl is pursued by a hack journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Multi-faceted' looks like a description of the girl; it describes a gem cut with many facets.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose cut is a style of gem cutting with a flat base and a domed top covered in triangular facets.

clue.text: Books spell with hospital to overcome acute disorder

indicators.note: the hospital letter gets over the jumbled word, coming after it

parts.note: a hex is a magic spell or curse

indicators.note: disorder signals the letters of acute being jumbled

explanation.surface: A magic spell, with hospital help, cures a sudden illness, according to old books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges ACUTE into ATEUC, and 'to overcome' means the H gets past it, at the end. The books are the first six of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hexateuch is the scholarly name for the opening six books of the Bible taken as a unit.

clue.text: Routed and drained: appeal's reportedly going in

indicators.note: the sound-alike piece is placed inside the word for drained

parts.note: to bleed is to drain, as of blood or money

indicators.note: reportedly means we take the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: IT is sex appeal, so appeal's gives its, spoken with a buzzing final sound

explanation.surface: An army beaten and exhausted: their plea for mercy is going in.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is old slang for sex appeal, and 'reportedly' makes 'it's' sound like a Z ending, ITZ.
explanation.definitionFit: Blitzed can mean overwhelmingly defeated or destroyed by an all-out attack, as a routed force is.

clue.text: Former president's fallen dead out of rage

indicators.note: out of signals that the letters for rage are taken from the words before them

parts.note: a fad is a craze or passing rage; that the letters left also run unbroken inside the words fallen dead is a coincidence, as the F, A and D come out scattered

explanation.surface: A one-time leader has killed in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The F, A and D are scattered: F at the start, then the final A and D of 'dead'. Salvador Allende was president of Chile, overthrown in 1973.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was the Chilean head of state from 1970 until the 1973 coup.

clue.text: Good boy finishes off his dark port

parts.note: Dan is a boy's name

indicators.note: the closing letters of the words his and dark are taken

explanation.surface: A well-behaved lad completes some sombre task of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Baltic seaport city in northern Poland.

clue.text: Using room to puzzle out jumbo

indicators.note: to puzzle out here is to work the letters around until they make a new word

explanation.surface: A huge task: using the room to solve a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' looks like an elephant but is the adjective for huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginormous is slang for enormous, and jumbo also means extremely large.

clue.text: Allowed to wear articles such as long jumper

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in English

indicators.note: wearing something puts it on the outside, so the articles go round the word for allowed

parts.note: the is the definite article in English
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Permitted to dress in sportswear, as a long-distance runner might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long jumper' is one example of the answer, a track-and-field competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A long jumper competes in track and field, so is a sportsperson of that kind.

clue.text: Leader of patrol stopping group on artillery ranges

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next
stopping means plugging a gap, so the patrol's leader sits inside the group

parts.note: a sect is a group, especially a religious one

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word patrol is taken

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: A patrol's leader halts a unit on the artillery ranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ranges' suggests firing ranges; here it means bands of colours or frequencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are ranges of wavelengths or frequencies, as of light split by a prism.

clue.text: Figure maybe gravedigger's buried wrong one

indicators.note: something buried is put inside, so these letters go within the gravedigger

parts.note: a sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally included digging graves; the 's stands for has
ill can mean wrong or harmful, as in ill-gotten
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A gravedigger has put the wrong body in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure maybe' marks the answer as one example of a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextillion is a very large number, ten to the twenty-first power in modern usage.

clue.text: Squandering capital, one easily influenced lawyer's clerk

indicators.note: losing the capital letter means dropping the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a sheep is someone who meekly follows others

explanation.surface: A gullible spendthrift wastes his money and works as a legal clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk to the lawyer Wickfield in Dickens's David Copperfield. 'Squandering capital' looks financial; here it removes the first letter, S.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's novel the character works as clerk in a solicitor's office, so the name fits a lawyer's employee.

clue.text: Picking up, if not actually busy

definitions.text: Picking up, if not actually busy

parts.words: Picking up, if not actually busy
parts.note: picking up is slang for arresting someone, and busy is British slang for a police officer, so this is an arrest made by someone who is not a policeman

explanation.surface: Someone picks things up while not really being occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' looks like an adjective meaning occupied; it is the British slang noun for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Any member of the public may lawfully detain a suspect in some circumstances, a power not reserved to police officers.

clue.text: Turned off, keeping left, in slow movement

indicators.note: the jumbled word holds the letter for left inside it
off signals the letters of turned going wrong and being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turned off the road, staying left, and crawled along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TURNED into TRUNDE, and 'keeping' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to roll or move along heavily and slowly, so the noun is a lumbering motion.

clue.text: Idler gets by up in city areas

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the city and areas

parts.note: zones are areas or regions

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lazy person passes through parts of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BY into YB in this down clue; 'city areas' looks like one phrase but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is an informal word for a work-shy, indolent person.

clue.text: Warning wife's kept back as predicted

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning to people in the path of the ball

indicators.note: back tells us to read the wife and the following word from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A warning that a wife was being held back turned out as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' turns W and AS round to give SAW. 'Warning' is the golfer's shout of fore.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to know beforehand that it will happen, the same as forecasting it.

clue.text: New moon's fast drifting off

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the following letters

parts.note: the possessive is read as moons, giving its letters
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Fasting under the new moon, someone nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New moon' looks like one phrase; 'New' alone rearranges MOONS into SOMNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means sleepy or drowsy, on the point of nodding off.

clue.text: Form in music school, Australia, back queen visiting

indicators.note: the queen drops in among the other letters, sitting inside them
back tells us to reverse the word for Australia

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A queen drops in on a music school in Australia to see a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form in music' looks like a description of the school's lessons; it is the definition. 'back' reverses the nickname for Australia, and 'visiting' sets the queen inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, often playful movement in a symphony or sonata, a recognised musical form.

clue.text: Beer drinking girl in clubs — word finally got round

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the beer drinks in the girl, holding her inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
Jo is a girl's name

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A girl in a nightclub is drinking beer, and in the end word went round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got round' looks like part of the story; it is the definition, meaning persuaded.
explanation.definitionFit: To get round someone is to coax or wheedle them into agreeing, which is what cajoling means.

clue.text: Mammal, European, died in grip of mate

indicators.note: the mate holds the letter for died, gripping it inside

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: A European animal died held tightly by its partner.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA for mate comes from Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an egg-laying mammal of Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Strip that a rhymester got for Christmas?

definitions.meaning: a narrow strip of land joining two larger areas

definitions.text: that a rhymester got for Christmas?
definitions.meaning: a poet hunting for a word to rhyme with the festive season would come up with this geographical term

explanation.surface: What did a poet unwrap on the twenty-fifth of December?
explanation.walkthrough: 'got for Christmas' suggests a present; it means the word a rhymester finds as a rhyme for 'Christmas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical neck of land, such as Panama's, is a narrow strip connecting two land masses; it is also a near-rhyme for the festive season.

clue.text: Where to look for navel examinations?

definitions.text: Where to look for navel examinations?

parts.words: Where to look for navel examinations?
parts.note: navel-gazing is introspection, looking in towards oneself, and the phrase also suggests medical checks done in hospital wards

explanation.surface: A medical question about where belly-button checks take place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navel' sounds like 'naval', suggesting the forces; navel-gazing means looking at oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at one's navel means turning one's gaze toward the self, towards the inside.

clue.text: American vessel coming in charged for silk

indicators.note: the ship comes into the word for charged, sitting inside it

parts.note: tore means rushed or charged along
USS (United States Ship) prefixes American naval vessels

explanation.surface: An American ship docks and is billed for a cargo of silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like billed; it means rushed, TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse, tawny silk from the cocoons of wild Indian silkworms.

clue.text: Blue with cold, boy so dressed?

parts.note: sky blue is a colour, and the sky is blue
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is shivering and blue with cold because of how he is dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means naked, clad only in the sky, which explains why the boy is blue with cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyclad means naked, wearing nothing but the open air, and the question asks what clothing turns a boy blue.

clue.text: Wayne gets a suntan in the American air

parts.note: the film star John Wayne supplies his first name
when someone suntans, their body browns, read here as a phrase

explanation.surface: The cowboy actor bronzes himself in the sunshine of the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like the atmosphere; it means a tune or song.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous American marching song from the Civil War era, and an air is a melody.

clue.text: Copper hull got round lake

indicators.note: the hull surrounds the letter for lake, which sits inside it

parts.note: a pod is the hull or husk of a pea or bean

explanation.surface: A ship's copper-bottomed hull sailed around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests the metal on a hull; it is slang for a policeman, and PLOD is British slang for the police, from Mr Plod in Enid Blyton's Noddy books.
explanation.definitionFit: A plod is a British slang term for a police officer, especially a slow, uninspired one.

clue.text: Unlikely worker we enrolled for training

indicators.note: training puts the letters through a drill that rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A person who won't amount to much has signed up for a training course with us.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is an idle, feckless person, hardly someone likely to work.

clue.text: Modern service for the people who buy plugs?

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the modern era of dates
a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A new form of service for those who buy electrical fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugs' suggests electrical fittings; it means advertising plugs, as in plugging a product.
explanation.definitionFit: The admass is the section of the public easily swayed by advertising and mass-media promotion.

clue.text: Agreed when given bouquet to remove cape

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

indicators.note: the letter for cape is taken away from the perfumed word

parts.note: something given a bouquet or fragrance is scented
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: A woman said yes when handed a bunch of flowers, provided she could take off her cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers but means a smell, as of wine; 'cape' looks like a cloak but is the map abbreviation C.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to express agreement or consent to a proposal.
